name: BBQ Pulled Pork Rice Bowl
intro_html: This is comfort food that basically cooks itself. You load the slow cooker in the morning, and by dinner you have tender BBQ pulled pork piled over rice with sweet corn. One batch fills 14 containers, so a week of lunches and dinners is done in a single afternoon.
ingredients_display: BBQ Sauce (Sugar Free) (Sweet Baby Ray's): 1 bottle (450 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 5 cups (840 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (common in rub) (4 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: BBQ Sauce (Sugar Free), 1 bottle: ~$2.76. Buy 1 (covers this batch).
Rice, 5.5 cups dry: ~$1.23. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 2lb bags.
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn, 5 cups: ~$1.59. Buy 2 cans: $1.64.
Pantry seasonings (garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika, salt, black pepper): ~$0.58. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $26.38 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.88 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $26.43 across 14 servings, roughly $1.89 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $8.18 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $34.61. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
shop_smart: Buy the pork on sale. Pork tenderloin and pork loin go on rotation often. When you see a good price per pound, grab it and freeze until slow-cooker day.
Check the BBQ sauce label. Sugar-free sauces vary a lot in price. The store brand is usually a dollar or two cheaper than the name brand and tastes just as good under all that pork.
Rice and canned corn are your budget anchors. Buy the big bag of rice and stock up on canned corn when it drops below a dollar a can. These stretch the meat and keep the cost per bowl low.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot on a kitchen scale and write the number down. You will need it to portion evenly at the end.

Trim the pork tenderloin of any silverskin and excess fat, then lay it in the slow cooker. Pour in the chicken broth and season with garlic powder, onion powder, and smoked paprika, plus a little salt and pepper.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 hours, or on high for 3 to 4 hours, until the pork pulls apart with almost no effort.
Lift the pork out and shred it with two forks. Skim off most of the cooking liquid, then return the meat to the pot with a splash of that liquid to keep it juicy.
Stir in the sugar-free BBQ sauce until every strand is coated.
Meanwhile, cook the rice according to the package. Drain and warm the sweet corn.
Combine the rice, corn, and saucy pork in your weighed pot and fold everything together.
portion_html: Weigh the full finished pot, subtract the empty pot weight you wrote down, and divide that number by 14. Scoop that same weight into each of your 14 containers so every bowl is even.
credit_html: Recipe adapted from Skinny Fitalicious, rebuilt for 14-serving budget meal prep with weighed portions and Omaha pricing.
upsell_html: That is a whole week of hearty dinners sorted in one afternoon, cheap, filling, and something you will actually look forward to opening at lunch. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
